prerequisites: Thermodynamic cycles (Beau de Rochas, 1st and 2nd Diesel, Sabathé).
Mechanical and kinematics aspects of the engine.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide knowledge on reciprocating machines (basically Internal Combustion Engines and reciprocating compressors and pumps).
Analyze thermo-fluidodynamic aspects with the aim of investigating the main design criteria and how to analyze the machine performance.
Ability to carry out engineering projects while working in a multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to apply one s knowledge in thermo-fluid-dynamics and machine engineering to solve problems in theoretical and applied thermodynamics, fluid dynamics and heat transfer.
Ability to perform mechanical and thermo-fluid design of components, from basic aspects through to implementation.

Ability to analyze and model mechanical/electrical/propulsion components and systems: problems and models underlying industrial engineering, with particular reference to mechanical and energy engineering.
Advanced ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, procedures and methods, including the use of theoretical models, with awareness of their limitations and potential.
Ability to critically evaluate data and results and draw appropriate conclusions, being aware of the level of uncertainty that may affect them.
Ability to achieve preparation adequate for access to third-cycle studies (attendance at second-level masters and doctoral schools) to further deepen knowledge and skills in research.
Ability to identify, formulate and solve industrial engineering problems, particularly in the energy field.
Ability to design, analyze, plan and manage energy conversion systems, and their environmental impact, as well as service and process plants, including complex and/or innovative ones.

Deep knowledge of the theoretical and scientific foundations of engineering, both in general and specifically in the areas of energy and electrical engineering, enabling the identification, formulation and solution of complex problems or problems requiring an interdisciplinary approach.
Knowledge of methods for planning and carrying out highly complex experimental activities for the analysis of components and systems.
Knowledge of advanced design tools (mechanical, thermo-fluid-dynamic, electrical or multi-physics) for the modeling and numerical simulation of components or systems.
Applied fluid dynamics and machinery: machine components and energy conversion systems, propulsion systems and design principles.
Knowledge of electric machines and their power systems for traction. Knowledge of the structural and thermo-fluid-dynamic aspects of internal combustion engines.
Knowledge of the thermodynamic, thermo-fluid-dynamic, thermo-chemical and electrical phenomena underlying the main energy conversion systems.
Ability to independently analyze data and information, draw objective conclusions and make consequential decisions.
Ability to work in a coordinated group, with a clear understanding of the engineering problem s context and the interdisciplinary implications of the application area.

Autonomy in meeting commitments and deadlines, including the ability to allocate time and available resources to meet deadlines, to accurately assess one s own capabilities and resources to ensure commitments are realistic and achievable, and to prioritize activities based on importance and timing.
Ability to identify the need for new knowledge.
Ability to communicate and transfer information, ideas, problems and solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Ability to present professionally problems, solutions, analyses and results through written reports and oral presentations.
Skills in graphical representation and communication (preparation of diagrams, charts and tables).
Ability for autonomous and continuous learning and professional updating in the relevant engineering field.
Conducting bibliographic research using major resources (libraries, scientific databases, etc.).

Knowledge of theoretical and applied thermodynamics, energy systems, fluid dynamics, and the models used to describe them. Knowledge of systems and machines for energy production and conversion, with particular reference to turbomachinery and industrial combustion systems. Understanding of the role of different energy technologies in ensuring environmentally and economically sustainable energy production.

Ability to select and apply appropriate analytical, modelling, and experimental methods to design, analyse, and test fluid machinery, thermal engines, and energy conversion systems. This includes the functional design of internal combustion engines and the evaluation of their energy, economic, and environmental performance.
Ability to analyse data and information using established methods, interpret results, and draw consistent conclusions, also with the support of provided guidance.
Ability to compare alternative engineering solutions and contribute to technically justified decisions by referring to engineering standards and established industrial procedures.
Ability to work collaboratively and effectively within a team, understanding the engineering context and recognizing the main interdisciplinary implications.
Ability to organize one's work while meeting deadlines, managing time and resources effectively, and contributing to task prioritization.
Ability to recognize personal knowledge limitations and the need to acquire new competencies by identifying appropriate information sources.
Ability to communicate and convey information, ideas, problems, and solutions in engineering contexts to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, using appropriate technical language.
Ability to present engineering problems and results clearly and systematically through written reports and oral presentations, following standard formats.
Ability to graphically represent and communicate technical data, results, and solutions through the preparation of drawings, diagrams, graphs, and tables.
Ability to acquire and update knowledge in the relevant engineering field, independently, although primarily under guidance, using established educational resources.
Ability to identify and consult bibliographic sources and technical documentation (libraries, databases, manuals, and digital resources) with appropriate guidance.
Ability to learn through project-based and Problem Based Learning (PBL) methods, applying acquired knowledge and tools to case studies and real-world problems.
Ability to understand and interpret the basic principles of design, production, and maintenance processes, operating in compliance with quality, safety, and technical standards (ISO, UNI, etc.).

syllabus_topics: Fields of employment, typical parameters, geometrical and cinematic quantities.
Indicated and effective quantities, characteristic curves, user-ICE coupling, ICE-vehicle integration.
Influencing terms of intake process in 4 and 2 strokes engine.
Power control and regulation: partial load working condition
Overview on the main systems for fuel supplying: indirect and directed injection of the fuel; carburetor.
Charge motion analysis: flow characterization - swirl, tumble, squish.
Spark ignition combustion: flame propagation, heat release law formulation, anomalous combustions.
Auto-ignition combustion: delay time for ignition, heat release law formulation, direct ignition systems (Common Rail, pump injector).
Volumetric machines: Fields of employment, typical parameters, geometrical and cinematic quantities.
Volumetric machines: Indicated and effective quantities, characteristic curves.
Volumetric machines: Power control and regulation
Volumetric machines: Overview on the main applications
Volumetric machines: Automatic valves in reciprocating compressors

assessment_methods.method: Oral examination (questions on three topics, with support of paper for diagrams, formulas, and graphs)

assessment_rules: The oral examination verifies understanding, assimilation of topics, ability to graphically represent and communicate technical concepts, connection of subject areas, and use of appropriate technical language. Grading ranges from Fail (Insufficient) for serious conceptual errors to 29-30 and Honors (Lode) for complete, in-depth knowledge and critical thinking. Honors is awarded for brilliance and originality exceeding standard expectations. A minimum of 18 is required to pass.
